# 4-Week Intensive Course Schedule (Summer 2026)

**Course Format:** 20 business days (Mon-Fri), May 18 - June 12, 2026
**Daily Engagement:** 112.5 minutes (videos + Colab notebooks + exercises + quizzes + project work)
**Instruction Style:** Micro-videos (≤12 min) + Google Colab notebooks with Gemini AI assistance
**Fridays (Days 5, 10, 15, 20):** Synchronous 112.5-minute lecture (recorded) — covers weekly topics, project milestones, Kaggle competition, and Q&A. Pre-recorded micro-videos remain available for review.

::: below-table

**Note:** All notebooks are designed to run in Google Colab with Google Gemini AI assistance for guided "vibe coding" (draft → verify → document).

## Project Milestones (individual or pairs)

- **Week 1 (Day 5):** Proposal + dataset selection (1-page proposal + dataset link + target + metric + split plan + leakage risks)
- **Week 2 (Day 10):** Baseline model + evaluation plan (baseline pipeline + metric + split/CV design + baseline report table)
- **Week 3 (Day 15):** Improved model + interpretation (updated comparison, champion choice, importance + PDP/ICE, error segment findings)
- **Week 4 (Day 20):** Final model + executive-ready deliverable (final run-all notebook + model card/limitations + monitoring plan + slide narrative + 5-minute research presentation video)

## Kaggle Case Competition (individual or pairs)

- **Competition:** Summer 2026 MGMT47400 Case Competition: Bank Churn (predict customer churn probability, AUC-ROC)
- **Deadline:** Fri June 12, 2026 at 11:59 PM (Kaggle + Brightspace code submission)
- **Grading:** At least one submission (30% of competition grade) + leaderboard ranking (70% of competition grade)

## Core Course References

- **James, Witten, Hastie, Tibshirani.** *An Introduction to Statistical Learning* (ISLP) + Python labs. Download: [https://www.statlearning.com/](https://www.statlearning.com/){target="_blank"}
- **Hastie, Tibshirani, Friedman.** *The Elements of Statistical Learning* (ESL).
- **Provost, Fawcett.** *Data Science for Business*.
- **Pedregosa et al.** "Scikit-learn: Machine Learning in Python." *JMLR*.
- **scikit-learn User Guide** (pipelines, preprocessing, model selection, metrics, inspection).
- **Chip Huyen.** *Designing Machine Learning Systems* (deployment thinking, monitoring).

:::
